paragraphs: The X1 xDrive20i has been a mainstay of the X1 diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F48 models from 2012 to 2015 use the N47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's part of a family known for a specific timing chain issue. From late 2015 onwards, across both the F48 and later the F48, the X1 xDrive20i switched to the B47, a newer, significantly more reliable unit that doesn't share the N47's timing chain concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The X1 xDrive20i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 1.5-litre three-cylinder petrol fitted to the X1 sDrive18i from 2015 to 2022 (F48). This is a modern engine from BMW's B-series family, generally considered reliable. We replace timing chain components, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every B38 rebuild.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol fitted to the X1 xDrive20i from 2015 to 2022 (F48). Like the B38, it's a B-series unit that shares its core design and reliability characteristics. We replace timing chain components, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every B48 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the sDrive18i and xDrive20i are distinct models within the X1 range, and because they use different engines (B38 vs B48), it's important to confirm your exact engine code before any work begins. We verify:
